hook: Miles Brundage is an AI policy researcher who spent six years at OpenAI working on how the world should prepare for increasingly capable AI systems. He holds a BA in political science from George Washington University and a PhD in the Human and Social Dimensions of Science and Technology from Arizona State University, completed in 2019, with earlier stints at ARPA-E and the Institute for Human and Machine Cognition. From 2016 to 2018 he was a research fellow at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute before joining OpenAI in 2018 as a research scientist on its policy team. Over six years there he rose to head of policy research and then senior advisor for AGI readiness, leading the company's external red-teaming program and developing its first system cards for documenting model capabilities. He left OpenAI in October 2024, saying he wanted to influence AI's development from outside industry, and went on to found AVERI, a nonprofit focused on independent AI policy research, while advising organizations including the Institute for Progress, CNAS, Epoch AI and RAND.

standing.record: The site's records for Brundage add up to a policy career at OpenAI and a post-OpenAI nonprofit and advisory portfolio. The only company listed for him is OpenAI, a San Francisco startup founded in 2015. The lawsuit records list eight matters, seven involving OpenAI entities and one involving Anthropic. Those cases include United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc. and Many Worlds 2T Innovations LLC v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC. Each is marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. None of the entries names Brundage himself, so the pattern is a policy figure tied to OpenAI through his former role while the site's litigation record sits at the filing stage.
standing.standing: Miles Brundage stands outside industry in the records, as an AI policy researcher who left OpenAI in October 2024 after six years. He founded AVERI, a nonprofit focused on independent AI policy research, and advises the Institute for Progress, CNAS, Epoch AI and RAND. The site also lists him as a non-resident senior fellow at the Institute for Progress and an advisor to Epoch AI and RAND. At OpenAI he rose to head of policy research and then senior advisor for AGI readiness, leading external red-teaming and developing the company's first system cards. The site's company record still lists OpenAI as a company where he is an executive, even as the profile describes his departure. His current influence, as the records show, runs through AVERI and those advisory roles rather than through an operating AI company.
